parsed.explanation: A thin-data absolute monarchy that criminalises same-sex conduct, offers no gender recognition, denies LGBTI organisation registration, and has no discrimination remedies: structurally hostile with essentially no recourse if a visitor is outed. Against this, the record documents partial social visibility — a police-escorted Pride, virtual Pride without incident, a welcoming church, state HIV outreach to same-sex couples — and no documented enforcement of the statute against gender-nonconforming people, no trans-specific border rules, and no current trans-specific violence. Dated killings (2015) are isolated incidents. Extrapolating from criminalisation plus closed civic space but weak documented enforcement, the case sits in the Elevated band's upper half.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry, visa or screening rule documented; how border officers treat mismatched documents is an unresolved open question in a state with no LGR and closed civic space.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document discrepancy would route into a criminal-law environment with no advocacy bodies to assist.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sodomy statute on the books for all; a trans visitor in a locally same-sex relationship falls under it; no documented enforcement practice or custody conditions.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented; rule of law is weak (Not Free, 17/100).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Criminal statute plus absent institutions means outing during any police contact carries unquantified but real escalation risk.

care_services.exposure: 2019 survey: 59% of LGBTQ respondents disrespected at public health facilities, 30% denied services; dated and LGBTQ-wide, but care-refusal risk is documented.
care_services.protection: 2013 health policy requires services regardless of gender/orientation; 2012 state HIV outreach to same-sex couples.
care_services.interaction: Policy protections sit beneath the unchanged criminal law and unenforced in practice per survey.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official hostility on record: ministers rejecting UN protection calls, officials calling same-sex conduct immoral; registrar refusing LGBTI registration on morality grounds, upheld 2022 though a 2023 supreme court voided one refusal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional association/privacy/expression protections acknowledged by High Court; 2017/2022 broadcasting guidelines bar orientation-based hatred.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Civic space closed generally; no national advocacy body exists to support an outed visitor.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for trans minors or travelling families; adoption ban is resident-facing only.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two dated killings (2015) in one town, individual incidents not a rate; no trans-specific violence rate; societal stigma documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Pride 2018 was police-escorted and declared a success; virtual Pride 2021 passed without incident.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police tolerated organised visibility, but no documented record of how police respond to anti-trans violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law covering gender identity; no advocacy organisations able to register; no realistic remedy if outed and targeted.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Broadcasting hate-speech guidelines; constitutional rights acknowledged in principle.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Supreme court 2023 voided one registration refusal but ministry still refuses; relief channel uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Less severe than 0.35-A: no documented universal-exposure register, border refusal mechanism or visitor-facing targeting; the criminal statute is not shown being enforced against gender-nonconforming people, and visibility events occurred without state suppression.

Roughly comparable to somewhat below 0.55-B: that anchor has structured administrative friction with appeal desks; here any exposure meets near-zero institutional remedy, but no visitor-facing exposure is documented at all.

Higher than 0.25-D: no documented entrapment, raids, blackmail or selective enforcement pattern; documented public visibility (Pride with police escort, health outreach) and some policy protections distinguish this dossier from an actively enforced morality regime.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines an unenforced-on-record criminal statute, an absolute monarchy with closed civic space, and no gender recognition, against documented pockets of tolerance: police-escorted Pride, state HIV outreach, a constitutional court acknowledging LGBTQ rights, and health policy barring orientation-based discrimination. No trans-specific traveller exposure — border rules, facility bans, custody practice or enforcement sweeps — is documented, and the violence record is two dated, isolated killings. Under thin-data extrapolation, structural criminalisation plus absent remedies resolve the score downward from a tolerance-based reading, while the documented non-enforcement and public-visibility record prevents it reaching the High Risk band.
